compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
`scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` (policy `d37e-4f64-3265-4f30`, wired at `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:172`) passes CLEAN on the current tree, yet the reconciler still mutates the tickets tracker outside the atomic locked transaction. It misses those writes by construction: rules R1 (raw `subprocess` git) and R2 (the wrapper names `run_git`/`run_git_write`/`_run_git`/`_git`) enforce the MECHANISM rule "no raw subprocess git", while the reconciler write seam is sanctioned at MODULE granularity — every mutation primitive in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/git_adapter.py` carries a function-level `# raw-git-ok: reconciler write seam (git_adapter/_ref_lock)` marker (`git_adapter.py:184`, `:230`, `:246`, `:252`). Because those primitives are sanctioned exports, ANY caller may compose them into a hand-rolled non-atomic sequence and the checker approves each call individually. The PROTOCOL rule — "tracker mutations go through the atomic transaction" — is unenforced. Proven live instance: `reconcile_helpers.py:226`/`:246` (`git_adapter.add` + `git_adapter.commit`) stage-and-commit against the tickets tracker with no lock and no atomic commit+push.

## Approach
Add rule **R3 (seam composition)** to the EXISTING checker rather than a new script, so one gate, one marker vocabulary and one CI wiring keep covering raw git writes. R3 re-scopes the sanction from "every export of the wrapper module" to "the transaction seams themselves".

R3 fires on a call to a git-adapter **mutation primitive** made from outside the reconciler write-seam modules. The primitive set is `add`, `commit`, `commit_tree`, `read_tree`, `rm_cached`, `update_ref`, `write_tree`. Read/query exports are excluded, and so is `commit_email`: despite its name it is `git log -1 --format=%ae` (`git_adapter.py:293`), a read.

Because `add`/`commit` are ubiquitous method names, R3 binds on the RECEIVER, not the bare attribute: a call fires only when the receiver is a resolved git-adapter module reference. Two binding forms, both already used in-tree, are resolved per file — an import binding, `from rebar_reconciler import git_adapter` (`__main__.py:321`, `apply_outbound.py:67`, `_concurrency.py:55`), including `as`-aliases; and a dynamic-loader binding, `git_adapter = _load("rebar_reconciler.git_adapter", "git_adapter.py")` (`reconcile_helpers.py:203`), recognised by the module-path string argument. A bare-name call also fires when the name was `from`-imported out of a git-adapter module. Anything else is not a git-adapter call and does not fire, so `set.add(...)` and `session.commit(...)` stay silent.

Sanctioned entry set (R3 never fires inside these): the reconciler write-seam files themselves — `git_adapter.py`, `_ref_lock.py`, `_ref_lock_push.py`. Those ARE the atomic transaction; the primitives are defined and composed there under the ref lock.

Sanction elsewhere reuses the existing inline `# raw-git-ok: <reason>` marker unchanged — line-level or enclosing-function, reason mandatory, no external allowlist file. Reusing it rather than minting a second marker keeps one sanction vocabulary, and the existing `marker-without-reason` violation then covers R3 for free.

**Riskiest assumption, checked first:** that R3's receiver binding yields no false positives across `src/` and `scripts/` — the rule is unusable if ordinary `.add(`/`.commit(` calls fire. The cheapest falsifying check is `--report` over the tree, confirming every new hit is a real git-adapter call; it runs before any marker is written.

## Scope
- `scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` — add R3: the primitive set, the per-file git-adapter binding resolver, the seam-internal file set, the emission, and the docstring policy. R1/R2, marker semantics and the fail-closed classes stay unchanged.
- `tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py` — R3 unit tests against synthetic trees.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile_helpers.py` — durable reasoned marker on `_commit_binding_store_snapshot`.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py` — durable reasoned marker on `_purge_committed_reconciler_locks`.

## Site dispositions (from the rule's first run; full evidence in a ticket comment)
Both remaining out-of-transaction sites take a **durable reasoned marker**, not a "drains later" debt baseline.

1. `reconcile_helpers.py:226/246` — `_commit_binding_store_snapshot`. Ticket `6454-d06e-7361-4e3d` was scoped to convert this and deliberately did not: routing through `rebar._store.push.commit_and_push_tickets_branch` (which stages `git add -A`) sweeps in `.bridge_state/last-pass.json`, which the selective 5-file staging excludes, advancing the tickets HEAD every idempotent pass and turning `test_reconcile_idempotency.py::test_unchanged_second_pass_preserves_binding_store_bytes_and_head` RED. The marker cites that boundary; follow-up `11a9-b11b-e93d-4832` owns giving the seam a pathspec so the marker can be deleted.
2. `__main__.py:338-351` — `_purge_committed_reconciler_locks`. Composes the primitives in a DETACHED temp index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE` set at `__main__.py:337`) and CAS-advances the ref (`update_ref(..., new_commit, old)`), so it never touches the worktree or main index and a concurrent writer is safe. Per-site marker rather than a blanket "detached-index is exempt" rule: detachedness comes from an `env` dict built at the call site, so it is not statically decidable from the callable, and a blanket rule would be forgeable by any future caller passing `env=`.

## Testing
Unit tests in `tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py`, driven against synthetic source trees as the existing tests are:
- **Fires:** a module doing `from pkg import git_adapter` then `git_adapter.add(d, "f")` and `git_adapter.commit(d, "m")` yields two `seam-composition` violations naming those primitives.
- **Sanctioned entry:** the same calls inside `git_adapter.py` / `_ref_lock.py` / `_ref_lock_push.py` yield zero R3 violations.
- **Marker semantics:** those calls with `# raw-git-ok: reason` on the line, and with it on the enclosing function, both pass; a bare `# raw-git-ok:` still fails as `marker-without-reason`.
- **False-positive floor:** `s = set(); s.add(x)` and `session.commit()` in a module with no git-adapter binding yield zero violations, as do `git_adapter.rev_parse(...)` and `git_adapter.commit_email(...)`.
- **Dynamic-loader binding:** `git_adapter = _load("rebar_reconciler.git_adapter", "git_adapter.py")` then `git_adapter.commit(...)` fires.
- **Whole-tree regression:** `check(REPO_ROOT)` returns no violations with the markers in place.

## Non-goals
Remediating the two sanctioned sites, changing `git_adapter`'s API, and runtime interception.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] R3 fires on a git-adapter mutation-primitive call outside the seam.
- [x] R3 does not fire inside the sanctioned seam files.
- [x] R3 does not fire on non-git-adapter `.add(`/`.commit(` calls or read-only exports.
- [x] A reasoned `# raw-git-ok:` sanctions an R3 hit; a reasonless marker still fails.
- [x] Both enumerated sites carry a durable reasoned inline marker, not a placeholder.
- [x] `check_raw_git_writes.py` reports zero unsanctioned violations.
- [x] `make lint` (incl. complexity ratchet) and `make typecheck` exit 0.
- [x] [operator-attested] The change lands at `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`.
      provenance: environment=Gerrit and GitHub Actions CI for navapbc/rebar; principal=rebar-review-bot and rebar-ci-bot service accounts, the only identities permitted to cast these labels; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — vote outcomes live in Gerrit metadata, unobservable from the repository.
      Observed: change 1916, LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, 0 unresolved, MERGED as 46b5d60f6f.
      Orchestrator re-verified on the merged tree: checker exits 0; 54 tests pass (42 before).
